# konnect_ai_cost_export (Resource)

AICostExport Resource

## Example Usage

```terraform
resource "konnect_ai_cost_export" "my_aicostexport" {
  compression = "gzip"
  dataset     = "focus"
  filters     = "{ \"see\": \"documentation\" }"
  focus = {
    charge_period = "day"
    tag_keys = [
      "..."
    ]
    version = "1.4"
  }
  format = "csv"
  from   = "2021-08-21T03:16:11.191Z"
  labels = {
    key = "value"
  }
  time_zone = "UTC"
  to        = "2022-12-17T02:42:17.591Z"
}
```

<!-- schema generated by tfplugindocs -->
## Schema

### Required

- `compression` (String) How the data files are compressed.

`none` or `gzip` for `csv`, and `zstd` for `parquet`.
possible known values include one of ["none", "gzip", "zstd"]; Requires replacement if changed.
- `dataset` (String) The data the export holds. possible known values include one of ["usage_events", "focus"]; Requires replacement if changed.
- `format` (String) The file format of the data files. possible known values include one of ["parquet", "csv"]; Requires replacement if changed.
- `from` (String) The start of the range, inclusive, as an RFC 3339 timestamp. The export holds the events whose `time` is at or after `from`.

At most 9 fractional-second digits.
Requires replacement if changed.
- `to` (String) The end of the range, exclusive, as an RFC 3339 timestamp. The export holds the events whose `time` is before `to`.

At most 9 fractional-second digits. It must be:

- after `from`.
- at most 13 calendar months after `from`, counted in `time_zone`.
- no later than the end of the day in progress in `time_zone` when the request arrives, so a range can include the day in progress.
Requires replacement if changed.

### Optional

- `filters` (String) Filters that select the events to export, with the same fields, operators, and shape as the `filters` of `POST /v1/ai-cost-management/events/query`. Every filter must match.

Defaults to `{}`.
Requires replacement if changed.; Parsed as JSON.
- `focus` (Attributes) The FOCUS options of a `focus` export.

Required when `dataset` is `focus`, and isn't accepted for any other dataset.
Requires replacement if changed. (see [below for nested schema](#nestedatt--focus))
- `labels` (Map of String) Key-value metadata on the export, set when it's created, or copied from the schedule that created it. The export list can filter by label. Labels don't change which events the export holds. Requires replacement if changed.
- `time_zone` (String) The IANA time zone that decides where each file's period starts: a day for a `usage_events` export, or a calendar month for a `focus` export. For a `focus` export, it also decides where the charge and billing periods start.

An IANA time zone name as the time zone database spells it, such as `Europe/Budapest`. Offsets such as `+02:00` aren't accepted. Defaults to `UTC`.
Default: "UTC"; Requires replacement if changed.

### Read-Only

- `created_at` (String) An ISO-8601 timestamp representation of entity creation date.
- `data_read_at` (String) When the successful attempt began reading the stored events, as an RFC 3339 timestamp in UTC. An event stored after this time can be missing from the files. Comparing the `data_read_at` and `record_count` of 2 exports of the same range and filters shows whether they differ.

`null` until the export succeeds.
- `expires_at` (String) An ISO-8601 timestamp representation of entity expiration date.
- `failure_reason` (String) Why the export failed. `query_limit_exceeded` means that reading the events took more time or memory than one export may use, so an export with a shorter range or narrower filters can succeed, and a `focus` export can also name fewer `tag_keys` or use `day` for `charge_period`. `attempts_exhausted` means that every attempt failed for a reason that a later attempt could overcome, such as an outage, so the same export created later can succeed. A schedule doesn't create a failed export again.

The set of reasons can grow, so a client treats a reason it doesn't know as a general failure. `null` unless `status` is `failed`.
- `files` (Attributes List) The data files, in date order. A `usage_events` export has one file for each day of the range in `time_zone`, and a `focus` export has one for each calendar month. The first and last files can cover part of their period, and a period without matching events still has a file, with no records. The list doesn't include `manifest.json`.

`[]` until the export succeeds. (see [below for nested schema](#nestedatt--files))
- `finished_at` (String) When the export succeeded or failed, as an RFC 3339 timestamp in UTC.

`null` until then.
- `id` (String) Contains a unique identifier used for this resource.
- `record_count` (Number) The number of records across all data files.

`null` until the export succeeds.
- `schedule` (Attributes) The schedule that created the export.

`null` for a one-time export, and once the schedule is deleted. (see [below for nested schema](#nestedatt--schedule))
- `started_at` (String) When the first attempt started, as an RFC 3339 timestamp in UTC.

`null` while the export is `pending`.
- `status` (String) Where the export is in its lifecycle. A client reads the export again with `GET /v1/ai-cost-management/exports/{exportId}` to follow its progress.
- `updated_at` (String) An ISO-8601 timestamp representation of entity update date.

<a id="nestedatt--focus"></a>
### Nested Schema for `focus`

Required:

- `version` (String) The FOCUS version of the files, which decides what their cost columns hold. possible known values include one of ["1.3", "1.4"]; Requires replacement if changed.

Optional:

- `charge_period` (String) The length of each row's charge period.

Defaults to `day`.
possible known values include one of ["day", "hour"]; Default: "day"; Requires replacement if changed.
- `tag_keys` (List of String) Tag keys whose values split the rows. Events with different values for a named key, or without the key, go into different rows. A row's `Tags` column holds the named keys that its events carry, with their values. A key with a different value for every agent session or CI run, such as `agent-session` or `ci-run`, makes about one row per session or run.

At most 64 keys, each listed once and following the tag key rules: 1 to 128 characters, each a lowercase ASCII letter, a digit, `.`, `_`, or `-`. Defaults to `[]`.
Default: []; Requires replacement if changed.


<a id="nestedatt--files"></a>
### Nested Schema for `files`

Read-Only:

- `name` (String) The file's name, which the download operation takes as `file`. A `usage_events` file is named by its day as `YYYY-MM-DD`, and a `focus` file by its month as `YYYY-MM`, both in the export's `time_zone`. The extension that `format` and `compression` set follows, as in `2026-09-01.parquet` or `2026-09.csv.gz`.
- `record_count` (Number) The number of records in the file.
- `sha256` (String) The SHA-256 digest of the file as downloaded. A client checks a download by comparing its size and digest with `size_bytes` and `sha256`.

64 lowercase hexadecimal digits.
- `size_bytes` (Number) The size of the file as downloaded, in bytes.


<a id="nestedatt--schedule"></a>
### Nested Schema for `schedule`

Read-Only:

- `id` (String) The identifier of the schedule that created the export, which the export schedule operations take as `scheduleId`.

## Import

Import is supported using the following syntax:

In Terraform v1.5.0 and later, the [`import` block](https://developer.hashicorp.com/terraform/language/import) can be used with the `id` attribute, for example:

```terraform
import {
  to = konnect_ai_cost_export.my_konnect_ai_cost_export
  id = "5f9fd312-a987-4628-b4c5-bb4f4fddd5f7"
}
```

The [`terraform import` command](https://developer.hashicorp.com/terraform/cli/commands/import) can be used, for example:

```shell
terraform import konnect_ai_cost_export.my_konnect_ai_cost_export "5f9fd312-a987-4628-b4c5-bb4f4fddd5f7"
```
